narrative.overview:
ActForGoa is a restrained, practical field guide. Warm paper, forest-green ink, upright Manrope, outline icons, and clear rules make the next step easy to find. Strong headings and large outlined choices provide hierarchy without decorative imagery or bright accent fields.

The visitor chooses a topic, identifies a need, and reaches a useful next action before browsing the related directory and reading. The menu should feel as direct as a public information kiosk, with plain words and generous targets. Original photographs continue to carry local character in the discovery feed and articles. Official Arc components provide the common controls and interaction behavior.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper, forest-green text, and a restrained neutral palette.
Upright Manrope with clear page, section, choice, and reading hierarchy.
Large outlined topic and action controls with Lucide outline icons.
Plain visible labels and a topic-to-need-to-action progression.
Original local photography in discovery and reading.
Shared Arc controls, stable text-field focus, and browsing continuity.

rules.name: The Restrained Colour Rule
rules.body: Use the documented green and neutral roles. Do not restore yellow or pink welcome fields, hero flowers, or filled pictorial illustration families.

rules.name: The Upright Type Rule
rules.body: Use upright text throughout, including wordmarks, quotations, labels, and numerals. Emphasis comes from size, weight, and space.

rules.name: The Reading Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Keep reading copy at 18px on phones and desktop. Separate headings through size, weight, and space; do not reduce body text to make more content fit.

rules.name: The Open Page Rule
rules.body: Content records, reading, and source context stay on the page ground with spacing and structural rules. Outlined topic and action choices are interactive controls, not a general card-container system.

rules.name: The Structural Line Rule
rules.body: Horizontal rules may separate records or sections; complete borders may identify controls. Never add decorative side stripes to content containers.

rules.name: The Choice First Rule
rules.body: Present the next understandable choice before directory records and reading. A visitor should not need to interpret a result list to discover what action to take.

rules.name: The Picture and Label Rule
rules.body: Pair outline icons with plain visible labels. Icons support recognition but do not replace accessible names or translated content.

rules.name: The Stable Focus Rule
rules.body: Text-entry focus changes fill and caret without a new border, visible ring, or size change. Links and buttons retain the Arc keyboard outline.

rules.name: The Source Proximity Rule
rules.body: Keep useful historical context and practical cautions near the information they qualify. Make detailed audit records optional; a prepared email is not a sent message.

rules.name: The Browsing Continuity Rule
rules.body: Preserve scroll position when filtering or resubmitting a search. Returning to a catalogue history entry restores its expanded results and chosen layout.

rules.name: The Reader Language Rule
rules.body: Show the person what to do, what to check, and where to go. Keep crawl dates, editorial review codes, and research-process language out of the primary guide flow while retaining useful cautions and optional audit detail.

dos: Do use restrained green and neutral roles, upright Manrope, and Lucide outline icons.
Do make topic, need, and next-action choices large and plainly labelled.
Do keep waste first among the eight home topics and treat wildlife help as one relevant need within its topic.
Do preserve original photographs in discovery and articles.
Do keep reading copy at 18px and provide a strong, consistent heading hierarchy.
Do preserve Arc focus, keyboard behavior, search, feed controls, and history restoration.
Do keep practical cautions and source access while making detailed audit material optional.
Do preserve original source files and keep phone data out of record presentation.
donts: Don't restore bright yellow/pink welcome fields, hero flowers, or filled illustration families.
Don't make snake rescue the default emphasis of the homepage or all-topic navigation.
Don't turn content records into enclosed panels because topic choices have borders.
Don't use serif, italic, or oblique type, decorative side stripes, or eyebrow labels.
Don't replace visible labels with icons or rely on colour alone for meaning.
Don't expose crawl dates, editorial check codes, or research-process language as primary reader guidance.
Don't invent biographies, photographs, contact details, service availability, or message-delivery claims.
